title: What the best settings for trading bots
author: ezztaxx
selftext:
I'm new into this, so I've got first and the main question:

Is it really possible to make a bot, which can start making money with low balance (\~100-200$) and make profits after \~3 months, and which candlelight setting better to choose (15min/1h/4h/24h), and can it do everything itself? Or is it too delusional?

Also, as far as I know, you need to put into the bot some data (but what data?), set the limits etc.

I've seen some post with starting balance of 50$ and immediate profit \~100$ a day.

So, what are your setting/criteria for trading AI bot? Which markets best to choose - crypto or stocks? And how to build strategy?

I appreciate everything you'd share🙏

comments.author: joshman1204
comments.body: No just save your money and invest in etfs it's a much safer bet.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
Taking your questions in order, since a couple have clean answers.

The 50 dollars into 100 a day post is the first thing to drop. At that balance the commission and the spread are a large fraction of every position, so the account can be right about direction and still shrink. Size is not something you tune later, it decides whether anything survives costs at all.

Timeframe is not a best pick from a list either. Shorter candles mean more trades, so costs land more often and each trade has to clear more before you see anything. Longer candles mean fewer trades and a much longer wait before you know whether the idea works. That tradeoff is the whole choice.

On data, start with the one series your rule actually reads. If you cannot say what the bot looks at and what would make it wrong, there is no strategy to automate yet, only an intention.

So the question I would answer first: what makes you close a position you already hold? That is the part beginners skip and the part that decides how this ends.

replies.body: Thank you for the response! Appreciate a lot! I'll take it into account

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body:
Anytime. The settings matter less than writing down why each one sits where it does, so when it stops working you know which knob you actually turned.

Which one are you changing first?

comments.author: ejpusa
comments.body:
Suggest ask AGI (Astra) your question; it's pretty helful.

___________

KALSHI WEATHER — WIDE-NET PAPER-TRADING EXPERIMENT

We need to change the operating philosophy of our Kalshi weather models.

PRIMARY OBJECTIVE

Our current problem is not that the models are trading too much.

They are trading far too little.

If the entire weather system runs for approximately 12 hours and produces only zero or one trade, consider that a FAILURE of the current experimental configuration.

We are still PAPER TRADING.

There is no real capital at risk.

This is exactly when we should be willing to widen the net, experiment, collect data, and find out where our models actually have predictive value.

Our new philosophy:

YOU HAVE TO BE IN IT TO WIN IT.

We want a FULL SLATE of legitimate experimental paper trades rather than waiting indefinitely for nearly perfect setups.

Do NOT make radical changes to the underlying forecasting science.

Instead, intelligently loosen the gates that are preventing otherwise reasonable predictions from becoming paper trades.

TARGET BEHAVIOR

Audit the complete pipeline:

weather data
→ forecasts
→ model predictions
→ Kalshi markets
→ candidate generation
→ filters
→ confidence
→ edge calculations
→ price limits
→ liquidity filters
→ settlement windows
→ ranking
→ trade eligibility
→ paper-trade execution

Determine exactly where potential trades are being eliminated.

We want substantially more candidates to survive this pipeline.

As an experimental target, each active model should generally produce at least one paper trade or a near-trade candidate during a normal 12-hour operating window when eligible markets exist.

Do NOT fabricate trades when there are no legitimate eligible markets.

But when legitimate markets exist, a model repeatedly producing nothing should be treated as something that needs investigation.

CREATE A WIDE-NET EXPERIMENTAL MODE

Implement a configurable mode such as:

WIDE_NET_PAPER_MODE=true

This must ONLY affect paper trading.

It must NEVER silently loosen safeguards for real-money/live trading.

When WIDE_NET_PAPER_MODE is enabled:

Lower overly conservative minimum confidence thresholds.

Lower minimum predicted-edge requirements moderately.

Expand acceptable Kalshi price ranges.

Allow somewhat longer-shot opportunities.

Expand the number of weather markets examined.

Expand geographic coverage where our data supports it.

Consider additional temperature/weather contracts compatible with our existing forecasting data.

Relax overly restrictive settlement-window filters where technically reasonable.

Increase the number of candidate markets retained before ranking.

Allow secondary and tertiary opportunities instead of taking only the single highest-confidence setup.

Examine BOTH sides of markets.

Do not accidentally create a structural bias toward YES/NO, OVER/UNDER, HOT/COLD, etc.

Allow models to trade their best available opportunity even when it would previously have been classified as a "lean" rather than a full trade — provided the signal is directionally meaningful.

USE GRADUATED TRADE TIERS

Instead of:

TRADE
or
NO TRADE

create something closer to:

TIER A — strong paper trade
TIER B — normal paper trade
TIER C — experimental paper trade
WATCH — near trade
REJECT — insufficient signal

Wide-net mode should allow Tier C trades.

We WANT to learn what happens to these weaker signals.

Tag every trade with its tier so we can later compare:

win rate
ROI
edge
model
market type
price
forecast horizon
confidence
signal strength

This lets the data tell us later whether our current conservative thresholds were justified.

MODEL PARTICIPATION

Every active weather model should be trying to participate.

For every 12-hour window calculate:

eligible markets examined
candidates generated
trades generated
near trades
rejected candidates
top rejection reasons

If a model generates ZERO trades despite having eligible markets available, explicitly report why.

Example:

MODEL: temperature_consensus_v3
Eligible markets: 31
Candidates: 14
Trades: 0
Near trades: 4

Top rejection reasons:
minimum_edge: 7
price_limit: 4
confidence: 2
settlement_window: 1

This information is critical.

We need to see what is choking trade generation.

BEST-AVAILABLE EXPERIMENT

Add an optional experimental mechanism for paper trading.

If a model has found legitimate eligible markets but none crosses the normal trade threshold, allow it to select its best available directional opportunity as an experimental Tier C trade when there is at least a minimally meaningful signal.

This is NOT a random trade.

There must still be:

a model prediction
a directional signal
a valid Kalshi market
valid market data
a rational relationship between forecast and contract
basic sanity checks

But we should not require extraordinary confidence.

Record:

best_available_trade = true

so these trades can be evaluated separately.

Do not force a trade if all signals are essentially neutral or the underlying data is invalid/stale.

DO NOT DESTROY THE EXISTING MODELS

This is important.

Do NOT rewrite the forecasting algorithms merely to create trades.

Do NOT artificially inflate confidence.

Do NOT fake edge.

Do NOT manufacture signals.

Do NOT remove data-quality checks.

Do NOT remove stale-data protection.

Do NOT trade invalid or closed markets.

Do NOT allow paper-trading changes to leak into real-money execution.

We are changing trade-selection aggressiveness, not corrupting the underlying forecasts.

KEEP CONTROL GROUP DATA

Where possible, record whether each wide-net trade would have passed our previous conservative rules.

For example:

would_trade_old_rules = true/false

This allows us to compare:

OLD CONSERVATIVE STRATEGY

versus

NEW WIDE-NET STRATEGY

without losing our baseline.

This is extremely important because after enough paper trades we can determine empirically where the optimal thresholds actually are.

DASHBOARD / TERMINAL

Add a simple Wide-Net report showing:

Last 12 Hours

Models active
Markets examined
Candidates
Paper trades
Tier A
Tier B
Tier C
Near trades
Models with zero trades
Average trades/model
Old-rule qualifying trades
Wide-net-only trades

Then show each model:

MODEL                     TRADES   NEAR   BEST SIGNAL

Model 1                     3       2       YES
Model 2                     2       4       UNDER
Model 3                     1       3       NO
Model 4                     0       5       OVER

Zero-trade models should be visually obvious.

EXPERIMENTAL GOAL

We need DATA.

A weather model that theoretically makes excellent predictions but almost never trades gives us very little information about whether it actually works.

Paper trading is our laboratory.

We therefore want to move from:

"Only trade when everything is nearly perfect."

to:

"Trade reasonable signals, categorize their strength, collect the results, and let the evidence tell us where the profitable boundary actually is."

Aim for a healthy, diverse slate of paper trades across the models and available markets.

Do not chase volume blindly.

But err deliberately toward PARTICIPATION rather than inactivity.

After implementing the changes:

Run the existing tests.

Add tests for Wide-Net mode.

Verify live-money safeguards remain unchanged.

Run the models against recent historical/current available data.

Show BEFORE vs AFTER trade counts.

Identify the filters responsible for the largest increase in trade opportunities.

Report any model that still produces zero or almost zero trades and explain exactly why.

Recommend the next SMALL threshold adjustment if trade volume remains too low.

Do not stop merely because the code compiles.

Validate that the change actually results in substantially more PAPER TRADES.

The objective of this experiment is simple:

CAST A BIGGER NET. GET INTO THE MARKETS. COLLECT ENOUGH TRADES TO LEARN WHAT ACTUALLY WORKS.
